ledger.claim: The governing measurement is the trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: under POL-RD-01 gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs wherever it disagrees with trip_record.actual_distance_km, and trip_record.actual_distance_km (14.3 km) may not be cited for the threshold test. The trace measures 14.31 km against a booked optimal of 2.4 km, an excess of 11.91 km — 496.25% of optimal. Both establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) and both materiality tests (greater than 50% and greater than 8.0 km) are passed, so a material route deviation is established on this trip's own trace.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, not discretionary: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 2.4 km + 0.28 x 5.0 min) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 7.80, against a charged_total of 21.35, giving a refund of 13.55 before rounding. That is far above the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor, and at 63.5% of charged_total it is below the 90% share that would convert the remedy to a full refund — so the rider's entitlement is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.55, payable rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05.

The surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.0, as POL-RD-02 requires; the trip_record does not carry the field at all and must not be used as its source. With a multiplier of 1.0 the surge neither inflates nor reduces the recomputed fare, and the 13.55 refund figure is therefore reproducible line by line from the fare_breakdown.

Nothing may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure: the fare carries zero ERP gantries (erp totals 0.00), no airport surcharge and no other fixed surcharge, so there is no pass-through line to correct and no risk of the double count POL-RD-09(1) forbids — any off-route ERP would already be comprehended inside the 13.55 refund, and here there is none.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07, so the measured excess stands and no straight-line substitute applies: 130 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds mean limbs (a), (b) and (c) are all unmet. Because the trace is not impaired, POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and this case is not one that must be escalated away from a monetary ruling for want of corroboration.

The rider discharges the initial burden that POL-RD-08 places on her: the same trip identifier TRP-02848 runs across the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown, and the pickup timestamp matches to the second — the first GPS fix at 2026-08-18T20:32:57+08:00 is the trip_record's started_at — and the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who must name a specific artifact and a specific clause to escape the arithmetic.

The driver's statement that 'the rider changed the destination verbally' names no artifact on this trip and cannot be run: POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor or within three minutes of it, identifying a place or road specifically enough to act on, and corroborated by the trace passing within 200 m of chat_message.waypoint_hint. EV-CHAT-02848 is a complete, untruncated log carrying zero messages and no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable on the record and, under POL-RD-14, an instruction the trace does not corroborate excludes no distance from the excess.

No relocation of either endpoint is recorded, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked optimal of 2.4 km remains the baseline: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff are both null, and the dropoff on the record is the originally booked Blk 25 Ghim Moh Link. A verbal assertion of a changed destination cannot substitute for the stored amendment timestamp and re-quote the clause requires.

No traffic advisory covers this trip and its absence is citable: EV-ADVIS-02848-01 is MISSING, carries the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and has weight_multiplier 0.0 (no advisory covers the Blk 640 Jurong West St 61 corridor in this window). With no advisory record naming a road the optimal route traverses and carrying a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached it, POL-RD-03 is unavailable and no part of the 11.91 km excess is exonerated; because the trace is unimpaired, POL-RD-13 leaves the deviation at the measured figure and runs POL-RD-02 against the booked optimal route.

The deviation is MATERIAL, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is mandatory — but it is run on the two fields that clause names and no others: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 210, so no pattern is established. Every other field on the driver profile is context only under POL-GEN-01, including the near-synonym lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags, which is not the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for and may not be substituted for it. ledger.claim: This dispute turns on a fact the record cannot reach, and that is a mandatory escalation rather than a ruling. The driver's answer is that the rider redirected the trip verbally, but EV-CHAT-02848 for this trip carries zero messages, so there is no rider instruction recorded, no waypoint_hint to test, and the 200 m corroboration test POL-RD-04 requires cannot be run at all; and EV-TRIP-02848 records no amendment whatsoever (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null) with amended_optimal_distance_km null, so the POL-RD-05 re-quote that would show whether the longer drive was to the rider's own revised destination is absent from the bundle. POL-RD-10(5) names this exact situation - an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that lacks the field the clause requires, its worked example being 'a rider-requested detour asserted with no chat_log for the trip' - so the Judge must not issue a final ruling. The trace itself is complete (130 fixes, 100% coverage, maximum gap 0 s, 10 s sampling), so the escalation is triggered by POL-RD-10(5) and not by POL-RD-10(3), and under POL-GEN-03 ESCALATE is terminal, holds the disputed amount rather than refunding it, and is exactly the disposal the driver asks for.

The remedy on this record cannot be uplifted to a full refund of the charged total, because the driver fails the POL-RD-06 pattern test decisively and in the driver's favour: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 210, so neither the '3 or more flags' limb nor the ratio limb is met (0 divided by 210 is 0.0, against the 0.05 threshold). No repeat-deviation pattern is therefore established, POL-RD-06(b)'s FULL_REFUND uplift is unavailable however the excess is characterised, POL-RD-06(c) supports no conduct referral against this driver, and POL-RD-06(a) resolves no finely balanced point against him. POL-GEN-01 makes those two trailing-90-day counters the only profile fields that may ground this test, and they ground it for the driver; the near-synonym lifetime counters on the same artifact point the same way and are not needed.

Even if the Judge rules money, the ceiling is a partial refund of SGD 13.55 - not the SGD 19.00 the rider contests and not the SGD 21.35 charged. EV-FARE-02848 records fare_model METERED, charged_total 21.35, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00; running the POL-RD-02 arithmetic on EV-TRIP-02848's optimal of 2.4 km and 5.0 min, with the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown itself, gives recomputed_fare of 7.80 ((3.80 + 1.80 + 1.40) plus the 0.80 platform fee) and 21.35 less 7.80 leaves 13.55. That is 63.5% of the charged total, below the 90% share at which POL-RD-02 would switch to FULL_REFUND, so the driver's maximum exposure on the rider's own best case is that capped figure.

There is no pass-through or billing-integrity component that can be added on top of any distance remedy, so the exposure cannot be inflated above the distance arithmetic. EV-FARE-02848 itemises no ERP gantry at all - erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00 and the off-optimal-route ERP total is 0.00 - and carries no airport surcharge line, so POL-RD-09(4) has no unmatched line to refund in full and POL-RD-09(2) has no off-route gantry to correct as a standalone pass-through. Every dollar in issue is distance and time, and distance and time are already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation; adding a separate ERP or surcharge figure would be precisely the double count POL-RD-09(1) forbids.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02848) governs the measurement, as POL-RD-01 requires, and it records 14.31 km against a booked optimal of 2.4 km (EV-TRIP-02848) — an excess of 11.91 km, 496.25% of optimal. The trace is complete — 130 fixes, 100% coverage, 10-second sampling, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s — so it is not impaired for policy purposes and the measured excess stands. Both establishment tests (>20% and >0.8 km) and both materiality tests (>50% and >8.0 km) are passed: the deviation is established and material. The trip record's rounded 14.3 km copy is not used for the threshold, and the fare breakdown's distance_charged_km (14.3) matches the trace.

Money (POL-RD-02, METERED fare). Charged total is SGD 21.35 (EV-FARE-02848). Recomputing on the optimal route: base 3.80 + 0.75 x 2.4 km (1.80) + 0.28 x 5.0 min (1.40) = 7.00, times the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (the trip record carries no such field), plus the 0.80 platform fee = recomputed_fare SGD 7.80. There are no ERP or toll lines (0.00), no airport or other fixed surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo, so recomputed_fare = 7.80. Refund = 21.35 - 7.80 = SGD 13.55, payable rounded up to the nearest 0.05 (13.55 already). That is above the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor and 63.5% of the charged total, below the 90% that would make it a full refund, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.55.

Driver's contentions. Your answer that the rider changed the destination verbally is not carried by any artifact. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02848) is in the pool, complete and untruncated, and holds zero messages; the trip record shows no amendment — pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-04's own rule for an unusable waypoint test says the clause is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses; POL-RD-05 is not engaged at all, because it applies only where an amendment timestamp is present, which it is not. So the escalation limb of POL-RD-10(5) is not triggered: the artifacts the clauses read are present and intact, they simply record nothing supporting the excuse, and an assertion citing no artifact cannot be invoked against one. Your points that the ceiling is SGD 13.55, that no pass-through amount may be added on top (POL-RD-09(1) — there is no ERP or surcharge line to correct or double count), and that no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral arises (deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 210 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern) are all accepted and are reflected above. No traffic advisory covers this trip (EV-ADVIS-02848-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), no party named one, and POL-RD-03 therefore exonerates nothing.

Rider's contentions. The burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: TRP-02848 matches across trip record, trace and fare breakdown, the first fix at 2026-08-18T20:32:57+08:00 is the recorded start time, and the excess is measured on an unimpaired trace; the driver points to no artifact in answer. Your reading of the trace field and of the surge source is correct, and your profile counters (1 deviation claim in 60 days, 0 substantiated) do not require corroboration beyond the trace. No profile field has been used to establish any fact about this trip or to carry a finding against either party; the two context-only fields mentioned (prior_deviation_flags, prior_no_show_flags) were cited only to say they may not be used.

Next step. The monetary effect, SGD 13.55, exceeds the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so this ruling issues but the amount is held and placed in the human queue for release rather than paid automatically. Confidence is 0.95, within the 1.0 cap set by the trace, trip record and fare breakdown that carry the deciding facts; the only sub-1.0 artifact is the missing advisory, which carries no fact and is relied on only for its absence.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
